title: Build, summarise and check your tracking sheet

say: Build, summarise and check your tracking sheet in Google Sheets.
This is the video for module 2 of Reporting and Performance Tracking.

Google Sheets is a free spreadsheet app that works on your phone. The golden rule is one row per record. Every row is one event, like one sale. Every column holds one kind of information, like the date or the item.
Use dropdown lists, so WhatsApp is always spelled the same way, and keep totals on a separate Summary tab.

say: Avoid empty rows, merged cells and totals typed in the middle of your data. And type numbers only, without the naira sign. These simple habits are what let formulas and charts work later.

say: Record each sale as soon as it happens. Entering a whole week from memory on Sunday night leads to missing sales.

say: Formulas always start with an equals sign, and recalculate by themselves when you add data.

panel.heading: Six formulas you will use most
items: Percentage change: new minus old, over old

say: SUM adds up your sales. AVERAGE finds the average sale. COUNTA counts how many rows you have.

panel.heading: Six formulas you will use most
items: Percentage change: new minus old, over old

say: COUNTIF counts matching cells, like orders marked No for unpaid. SUMIF adds only matching rows, like WhatsApp sales.

panel.heading: Six formulas you will use most
items: Percentage change: new minus old, over old

say: And percentage change is the new figure minus the old, divided by the old.

say: At the end of March, Bisi's SUM shows 280,000 naira in sales.
Her SUMIF splits it by channel: 142,000 on WhatsApp, 98,000 walk-in and 40,000 on Instagram.
These add up to 280,000, which confirms nothing is missing.

say: When a number is already a percentage, be careful. If conversion rises from 20% to 25%, subtracting gives 5 percentage points.
Dividing 5 by 20 gives a 25% increase. Both are correct, but very different.
The safe habit is to write: up 5 percentage points, from 20% to 25%. Then the reader sees the real change.
One duplicated row, or a price typed with an extra zero, can turn a weak month into a great one on paper. So check every week. First, turn on a filter.

say: Reconciling means checking your sheet against your money records.

card.title: Bisi reconciles with her payment app
card.note: The difference: one phone order never entered.

say: Her app shows 68,500 naira coming in. Her sheet shows only 63,500.

card.title: Bisi reconciles with her payment app
card.note: The difference: one phone order never entered.

say: The difference is 5,000 naira. She finds a phone order that was never entered, adds it, and notes the correction.
If personal money goes into the same account, keep a separate business account, or mark personal transfers clearly so they are not counted as sales.

say: To remember. One row per event. Use dropdowns, and type numbers without the naira sign. Let formulas do the counting. Be clear about percentage points. And check your data every week against your bank app, noting every correction.

panel.heading: Remember

SUM, COUNTIF, SUMIF and percentage change

say: Now practise. Build your Data tab with clear headings, dropdowns and five real records. Add a Summary tab with totals and progress against your target. Then run your first data check and start your Notes tab.
